claims.statement: EU NIS2 recitals state that the Union has faced an exponential increase in ransomware attacks and that Member States should develop a policy addressing the rise of ransomware attacks as part of their national cybersecurity strategy; the record is EU-scoped primary law and the source contract prohibits cross-jurisdiction generalization, so it remains contextual regulatory background and does not measure a directional change in ransomware incident count or frequency for the unscoped THREAT_RANSOMWARE NoI modality.

CISA KEV records that CVE-2022-27593, an externally controlled reference vulnerability in QNAP Photo Station, was observed being utilized in a Deadbolt ransomware campaign on 2022-09-08; the source contract permits only confirmed_exploitation and prohibits prevalence_magnitude and vulnerability_severity claims, so this is a single 2022 point signal and does not establish a directional change in ransomware incident count or frequency for the 2025-2027 forecast window.

IBM X-Force reports that ransomware constituted 17% of incidents remediated in 2022, had held the top action-on-objective spot since at least 2020, extortion was the most common attack impact at 27%, and phishing was the leading initial access vector in 41% of incidents; this is 2022 point-in-time incident-share context, not a measured directional change in ransomware incident count or frequency.

Mandiant M-Trends reports that the global median dwell time for 2022 was 16 days, down from 21 days in M-Trends 2022, and that intrusions involving ransomware had a median dwell time of 9 days in 2022 compared with 5 days reported in M-Trends 2022; this is dwell-time operational context, not direct evidence of ransomware incident count or frequency direction.

Crossref cutoff-constrained records report annual PMT_CRYPTOGRAPHY publication counts of 210 in 2021, 254 in 2022, 272 in 2023, and 330 in 2024, with an OLS slope of 37.8 works per year, and the record explicitly states it does not establish deployment maturity, operational effectiveness, or causal mitigation effectiveness; this is admissible as a directional publication-activity statement for the PMT NoP modality only and cannot serve as Attack stance-basis.

CISA CPG identifies ransomware among the cyber threats organizations face and presents prioritized cybersecurity practices aimed at reducing cyber risk; this is neutral defensive-context background without directional threat-trajectory content.

The supplied DBIR 2023 chunk discusses DDoS and DNS attack trends and includes the editorial observation that it was a respite to not have to write about Ransomware for a couple of pages; this is a qualitative editorial observation, not a measured incident count or frequency signal.

No remaining claim in the surfaced evidence set provides an admissible THREAT_TRAJECTORY statement on the THREAT_RANSOMWARE NoI modality. The structural absence of admissible threat-trajectory or gap-direction evidence means the Attack stance is neutral: neither the forecasted Threat NoI increasing direction nor the GAP_DIRECTION increasing direction can be affirmatively supported or challenged by the surfaced evidence under the strict NoI modality and source-contract boundaries.
